correctness.rationale: For every distinct vertex pair the nonresolving sets are precisely subsets of its equidistance bisector. Hamming distances decompose into independent three-atom signed coordinate variables. Conditioning on a >=4-letter factor bounds the center at its unique modal zero atom and is strict with other active factors; all-binary central binomial probabilities maximize only with exactly two active coordinates, and conditioning on a ternary factor bounds center mass by 1/3, with equality only for zero/one additional coordinate. Thus the six cases for the maximal bisector and all equality support types are exhaustive. Local pattern descriptions, intrinsic essential coordinates and distinct patterns give the claimed labeled counts. The actual attached executable was run on all 6 one-factor orders 2–7, 15 unordered pairs of orders 2–6, and 22 selected 3-to-5-factor cases; all comparisons passed. Finite tests supplement but are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original metric-dimension-threshold paper proves general properties and selected small graph families, but not mixed-alphabet complete-graph Cartesian products. The full Hamming graph resolvability paper tests specified resolving landmark configurations via algebraic constraints; no explicit universal threshold or classification/census of all largest obstructions was found. The 2026 equidistant dimension paper addresses the converse equality-of-distance condition for vertices outside a detector set. None of the inspected full primary results implies the new sharp six-case formula with all extremal bisector families and counts. Scope searches and accessible published-record comparisons did not identify stronger coverage; research priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The universal landmark count quantifies robustness to arbitrary sensor placement, in contrast to small specially designed metric bases. The theorem treats all Cartesian products of finite complete graphs (heterogeneous alphabets) and classifies every sharp obstruction with exact labeled count. Transitions between binary parity, ternary permutations, and two-forbidden-symbol slabs are structural and reveal information not present in the scalar threshold. At threshold minus one, the exact chance of a randomly sampled failure is A(G)/binom(N,M). These are complete natural invariant classifications; no broader general-graph conclusion is claimed.
